recipes.name: Andouille Sausage and Corn Chowder
ingredients_raw: 3 Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Cook and stir onion, bell peppers, and celery in hot oil until softened, about 5 minutes. Add sausage, garlic, and cayenne pepper; cook and stir until sausage is hot, 1 to 2 minutes. Stir in corn and bay leaves; season with thyme. Sauté until corn is warmed through, about 1 minute.
Pour broth into the pot; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low and cook at a simmer for about 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in potatoes and heavy cream. Cover and continue cooking at a simmer until potatoes are tender, about 20 minutes.
Season chowder with salt and black pepper. Remove and discard bay leaves. Garnish with cilantro to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Andouille Sausage and Corn Chowder
raw_recipe.description: This Cajun corn chowder is slightly spicy and smoky thanks to the addition of the andouille sausage and cayenne pepper.

review.reviewBody: Enjoyed this a alot although 2t dried thyme is WAY too much imo. I used just under 1t and it was still a bit too much. Followed the submitter's suggestion of adding a can of creamed corn - liked the texture much better. Thanks!

Excellent recipe! Would highly recommend. I omitted the cayenne pepper (didn’t have any on hand), used 3 fresh ears of corn instead of frozen, and followed the recommendations from others by decreasing the amount of thyme by half, and adding one can of creamed corn as a thickener. Turns out it still was not the thick consistency I was looking for in a chowder, so I made a simple flour slurry by mixing some of the soup liquid and two tablespoons of flour in a bowl, and whisked it into the simmering soup during the last 5 minutes of cooking to increase the soup’s viscosity. Worked perfectly! Next time I will omit the creamed corn all together and thicken the soup with the slurry. I didn’t need to add any additional salt or pepper as the sausage and chicken broth already provided enough seasoning. I also used half-and-half instead of whole cream, and omitted the cilantro (personal presence.) Delicious! Will definitely make this again!
Added three strips of bacon and sautéed onion and peppers in the drippings. Used extra potatoes and 2 sprigs of fresh time. Will be making this again.

Changed a couple things. Based on my spouse’s lactose intolerance, left out the cream. Used 1/3 cup of flour thickening and all the dinner guests were very complementary. Thanks for the recipe, now shared again.

This was delicious and my husband loved it. I used two full teaspoons of Tony Chachere's Creole seasoning instead of the cayenne (I am from Louisiana and we like spicy.) and since I didn't have heavy whipping cream, subbed a cup of milk with two tablespoons of corn starch. Will make this again.

Everyone loved it. Made exactly but did cut cayenne and thyme in half as others mentioned and used 3 ears of fresh corn that I had on hand. Grandson added 'Slap Your Mama' to his bowl since he loves the heat.

I've made this chowder twice and played with the seasonings. I like using fresh sausage but since it adds a lot of heat I cut down on the cayenne. I also took the advice of others and limited the thyme to 1/2 tsp which is just enough. My twist on this is to use sweet rather than white potato. Finally, I thicken the broth with flour and milk to give it more body. This is a great cold weather dish when you really want to have something hearty and filling.

I made this and I loved it. I used my own judgement regarding quantities and substituted milk for heavy cream. I made a slurry and added a little butter to achieve a similar richness. The aroma coming out of the kitchen as it was simmering was TO DIE FOR. This is a keeper.
I made this as a "Make ahead" meal, but used my crock pot! Save the heavy cream for the last hour. It's super easy and delicious!
I would agree with others than about a third less stock makes a better chowder. Otherwise I made it to the recipe. I like the cayenne and thyme in the recipe...gives it heat but also depth of flavor.

I will definitely make this again! I kept everything almost the same. The only difference was that I used half n half, 3 ears fresh corn, cut the thyme to 1/2 teaspoon, and made a medium roux with 3T butter and 3T flour. Added the roux at the very end stirring until slightly thickened. Amazing!

It was the perfect soup for our fresh garden corn, onion, bell peppers, Yukon gold spuds, celery and thyme. Wishing I could grow the Andouille also, but…😂 We were so pleased and thank you for the recipe, it is a keeper.
One of our favorites.
I did as a can of creamed corn but I followed the recipe exactly except that one addition. Delicious and will make it again. Served with a side of cornbread and a small salad.
Love this s stuff, corn chowder on a new level 😎

It's really good. I always laugh when people say they make a recipe, then change it. But I did ,lol. I omitted the thyme ( I don't care for the taste). Only used 4 cups of broth, and added a can of cream corn also. ( per, another reader's suggestion)

We really enjoyed this. I had to alter the quantities since there is only 2 of us. Had all the ingredients on hand and made as written. We will make it again but I think next time I will add a can of creamed corn to give it that thicker chowder consistency. A hit for us!
Basic bones was helpful to get me started, then I changed the whole thing up to make my tastebuds happy. Spices!! Heat!!
I use fresh corn off the cob, chicken andouille sausage, and evaporated milk. It’s amazing and I make it every year. Plan to freeze this batch, so I’ll have it in the winter.

This is delicious! Made as written with two minor substitutions: subbed peeled red potatoes for the yukon gold potatoes, and subbed 1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes for the cayenne pepper. Finished soup has the mildest hint of heat. Added 1 tsp kosher salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper when I dumped in the potatoes. I love as is, but can imagine a can of creamed corn would be a tasty addition, but really not necessary. I wanted something more light, but with the cream, and this fit the bill.
